method.cash: Cash view: venture rounds count the full round size, split evenly across the named lead investors (or labelled 'Lead not named'). Partnerships count only disclosed upfront payments. Acquisitions count the disclosed upfront price. IPOs count gross proceeds.
method.headline: Headline view: as above, but partnerships and acquisitions count their full reported value, including milestones that may never be paid.
method.scope: Named, sourced deals where AI is core to the company. This is a curated map, not a census: industry trackers count far more deals (see market context).

chains.title: Alphabet's AlphaFold bet keeps compounding

steps.label: Alphabet, GV & CapitalG join Thrive-led round
Next round in talks at a $40B+ valuation

chains.insight: Big tech money plus sovereign money (MGX, Temasek, UK Sovereign AI Fund) are funding the platform before it has clinical data. Pharma pays for access, and Gulf states offer data.

chains.title: Frontier AI labs buy into biology

steps.label: OpenAI's former science lead raises for Warp
Anthropic reveals it owns Mithril's drug programs

chains.insight: AI labs reach bio four ways: buying small teams, investing in model companies that sell to pharma, alumni who found companies, and owning drug programs outright (Anthropic–Mithril). Anthropic's S-1 now pitches that bio push to public investors. Most terms stay undisclosed.

chains.title: NVIDIA collects a toll on every layer

steps.label: Danaher builds NVIDIA AI into lab instruments

chains.insight: NVIDIA rarely leads a round, but it shows up in the cap tables of GPU-heavy companies, co-funds pharma's compute build-out, and now sits inside Danaher's lab instruments. With Iambic's IPO its portfolio is reaching public markets.

chains.title: Eli Lilly is investor, partner and customer at once

steps.label: Equity in Alchemab, NewLimit, Superluminal and BigHat

chains.insight: Lilly shows up in 8 deals on this map, more than anyone else. It takes small equity stakes early, then signs licensing deals with large milestone totals.

chains.title: Pharma money passes through AI biotechs

steps.label: Pathos pays Alphamab for the JSKN016 ADC

chains.insight: Some AI-first developers in-license assets from other biotechs (here Alphamab, a Chinese biotech), then raise from pharma to develop them. Investor cash goes to buying drugs as well as building models.

chains.title: Insilico turns one platform into many licences
chains.insight: About $6.3B in headline value but only about $152M in disclosed upfront cash, which shows how far pharma–AI deals are back-loaded.

chains.title: States are buying a seat at the frontier

steps.label: UK Sovereign AI Fund in Isomorphic and Basecamp

chains.insight: Sovereign and state funds mostly join late-stage rounds as co-investors and lead only small local deals. The pattern looks like industrial policy, with each country backing its own champions.

chains.title: AI money moves down the pipeline

steps.label: AstraZeneca joins Multiply Labs' robot manufacturing round
Lightspeed and Lux fund Warp's chemistry robots
BMS leads Pathos for AI-led trials
Boehringer and Microsoft test digital patient twins
Creandum seeds Atlas Bio's simulated Phase II trials
AstraZeneca and Oracle sign for AI trial recruitment

chains.insight: In October, money moved past molecule design toward delivery, lab and manufacturing robots, and now trial design and recruitment. Microsoft and Oracle are entering at the trial stage, where most R&D money is spent.
